findings.text: get_route_path puts root_path into a regex unescaped (re.sub(r"^" + root_path, ...)). A root_path with regex metacharacters, such as "/api(v1" or "/a.b", raises re.error or matches the wrong text, so "/aXb/x" is stripped as if it were under "/a.b". It also strips the prefix even when the path doesn't sit on a segment boundary. For example, root_path "/app" with path "/application" gives "lication". The fix is to use a literal startswith and slice.

_utils.py now imports starlette.types at module level. If starlette.types imports from _utils, or any module that does, this creates a circular import that fails at import time. It is also an unnecessary runtime dependency; a TYPE_CHECKING import would avoid it.
